text:
anya: quick sync — we need to decide scope and launch criteria for the auth changes in the new API surface (chat/completions, embeddings, tool-calls). customer asks are piling up from enterprise accounts. :thinking:

mike: +1. can we list the exact asks? i heard per-project keys, key rotation, and org-scoped roles. anything else?

anya: yeah — distilled asks: 1) project-scoped API keys (isolate billing + data), 2) org keys with role constraints (read-only vs invoke), 3) rotation workflow (grace window + audit trail), 4) SDK support for transparent rotation (refresh hooks), 5) explicit support for function/tool calling permissions.

sara: for tooling, note that tool/function calls must carry the same scope checks — e.g., a project-key can't call a tool it isn't allowed to. that's a major UX/compatibility risk.

raj: security perspective: mandatory rotation for high-priv keys, ability to revoke immediately, and immutable audit logs. also we should avoid any silent breaks for canary users — rotation must have dual-key acceptance window for a few minutes/hours.

oliver: infra notes: implementing dual-key acceptance impacts runtime auth check path. suggested approach: store active_keys + pending_keys with expiry in our auth cache. runtime check must consult cache quickly — want to avoid token DB hit on every request.

mike: launch criteria proposal: (A) API supports project and org keys, (B) rotation API with schedule + manual revoke, (C) console UI for key management, (D) SDKs with built-in refresh (opt-in), (E) permission model for function/tool calls. all must have basic e2e tests and perf < +5% latency.

anya: customers will push for shorter rotation windows. we should offer both: short-lived ephemeral tokens (default for hosted) and long-lived project keys (for legacy). ephemeral tokens address many security asks without breaking UX.

raj: +1 for ephemeral tokens. need KMS/HSM integration for private deployments. also require exportable audit logs to SIEM (syslog/s3).

oliver: perf tradeoff: ephemeral tokens require more frequent validation; we can validate via signed JWTs (locally verifiable) to remove DB roundtrips. recommendation: JWT for hosted, delegated introspection for Private.

sara: question on scope model: do we do hierarchical scoping (org > project > route) or flat role assignments per key? hierarchical seems more intuitive but adds complexity to checks and UI.

mike: product lean: implement flat scope for 1.0 (project-scoped + route-level allowlist), roadmap to add hierarchical RBAC in v2. Capture this in spec.

anya: sample header we discussed for dev docs:
```
Authorization: Bearer PROJECT_KEY_abc123
X-Org-ID: org_987
X-Project-ID: proj_440
X-Key-Scope: embeddings:read,completions:invoke,tools:call
```

raj: add an `X-Key-Version` header to help canarying and rollback. serverside accept both versions during transition.

oliver: for rollout plan: canary 5% of traffic -> 25% -> 100% across regions. automate fallback to old auth path if error rate spike > 2%. deploy-bot will trigger canary once spec branch is merged.

deploy-bot: deploy check: spec branch auth-gridwork -> lint OK, tests 82/84 passing, scheduling canary. :robot_face:

sara: tests we need: unit for scope parsing, integration for tool call permissions, perf regression test for runtime auth < +5% p50, and manual QA for console key UX.

mike: prioritization: must-have for enterprise customers with contracts (SOC2/PCI) = P0. Public SDKs + docs = P1 for GA. RBAC v2 = P2.

anya: action items: 
- oliver: prototype JWT-signed token validation and pending_key cache (due EOD Thu)
- raj: write security requirements for rotation (grace window, revoke semantics, audit exports) by Tue
- sara: draft test matrix and console UX mocks by Wed
- mike: update roadmap and customer comms + acceptance criteria by Fri

mike: team ok with that? :eyes:

anya: ok from me. we'll reconvene Wed AM for the UX review.

raj: ack.

oliver: ack, starting proto today.

sara: ack, adding QA tasks to squad board.

mike: thanks all. I'll prepare a one-pager for sales/solutions to set expectations. :thumbsup:
